extraction.name: C-E VAL
extraction.description: C-E VAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite comprising 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 diverse disciplines and four difficulty levels to assess the advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.publisher: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors selected subjects across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional) based on official Chinese educational and vocational directories. The questions were collected from mock exams in PDF or Microsoft Word formats and subsequently processed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of multiple-choice questions from mock exams formatted as PDF or Microsoft Word documents, covering 52 disciplines across middle school, high school, college, and professional difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The data was parsed and annotated by the authors into a structured format, which included converting complex mathematical notations into standard LaTeX. For the development split explanations, the authors prompted GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanations and then manually revised them.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotated questions underwent multiple rounds of human validation by the authors to check for quality and ensure LaTeX syntax compiled correctly.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to automatically generate initial step-by-step explanations for the answers, which were then manually revised.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited in scope as it primarily focuses on accuracy and does not evaluate other important LLM abilities such as API calling, safety, bias, and robustness.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster the development and improvement of foundation models specifically tailored for Chinese users by helping developers understand their models' capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of large language models (foundation models) in a Chinese context.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A public leaderboard is maintained on the benchmark's website to automatically evaluate and track test accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data manipulation included randomly dropping incorrect choices for questions with more than four options to standardize the format, randomly splitting the data into development, validation, and test sets, and augmenting the development split with step-by-step explanations generated by GPT-4 and human annotation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing steps involved converting PDF and Word documents into text, parsing questions into a structured format, manually converting complex mathematical notations into standard LaTeX, filtering out questions with fewer than four options, and applying a standard pipeline of deduplication, cleaning, and typo correction.

name.evidence: We present C-E VAL , the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models

description.evidence: C-E VAL consists of 13948 multiple-choice exam questions spanning 52 diverse disciplines, ranging from humanities to science and engineering... The questions are collected from four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional tests.

url.evidence: The C-E VAL data and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/hkust-nlp/ceval.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We also note that, C-EVAL, along with all the English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We anticipate C-EVAL will help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models, and foster their development and growth for Chinese users.
